deities: Chamunda Mata (fierce form of Goddess Durga/Shakti)

history.summary: FLAG - LOCATION: this temple is INSIDE Mehrangarh Fort at its southern end; it is not a standalone town temple. Coordinates are approximated to the fort's southern precinct (verify). Per local tradition Rao Jodha, founder of Jodhpur, installed his Isht Devi Chamunda's idol here in 1460 after bringing it from the old capital Mandore, to protect the new fort and city - following the legend of the displaced hermit whose curse threatened the fort with perpetual water scarcity. She remains the patron goddess of the royal family and of Jodhpur; legends credit her with shielding the city during the 1965 and 1971 Indo-Pak wars (unverified). The shrine has a white dome, carved ceiling and pillars.

name: Chamunda Mataji Temple
town_description: Jodhpur, the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City' of Rajasthan, is the historic capital of Marwar founded by Rao Jodha in 1459. Dominated by the massive Mehrangarh Fort, it is Rajasthan's second-largest city and a major tourist hub for Rajput heritage, blue-painted old-town houses, textiles, and handicrafts.
